conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be helping take care of you during your stay. You came in with worsening abdominal pain and vomiting—can you tell me more about what’s been going on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, thank you. The pain has been getting worse over the past week. It’s in my upper left and right belly, near my G tube. My usual morphine suppositories aren’t helping at all.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. And you mentioned vomiting every day for the last few days?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, daily for about a week now. Phenergan isn’t touching the nausea. I haven’t slept well because of the pain and vomiting.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That sounds really tough. We’ve reviewed your imaging—an X-ray showed some air-fluid levels, but no sign of a complete blockage. The surgical team doesn’t think you need surgery right now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s not another bowel obstruction?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not a complete one. It could be a partial slowdown, which fits with your history of sclerosing mesenteritis. We’ll manage your pain and nausea while keeping you on your TPN through your femoral line.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. My G tube output has also gone way up—1200 to 2200 cc a day. It used to be around 300.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, that’s consistent with increased gut activity or irritation. We’ll keep monitoring it. For now, we’re going to keep you NPO—nothing by mouth—so your gut can rest.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s fine. But please, I need better pain control.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Absolutely. We’re starting IV Dilaudid every 4 hours and IV Phenergan every 6 hours. We’ll watch how you respond and adjust as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I’ve been so frustrated. This pain is constant and nothing’s working like it used to.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I hear you. It’s a lot to manage. We’ve asked social work to check in with you—they can help with emotional support and coping strategies.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’d appreciate that. Sometimes the emotional pain feels just as bad.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How’s the pain now after the first round of IV meds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: A little better, maybe down to a 7 from a 10. But it’s still really uncomfortable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll keep the IV pain meds going and reassess. Your labs are stable—no signs of infection or kidney issues. We’ll continue TPN through your femoral line.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is my line okay? I’ve had problems with it before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We checked it. There’s tenderness near the site, but no infection. However, the external part of the catheter looks worn. We may need to replace it later.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Again? It’s split before in the same spot.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’re aware. It’s likely due to movement and positioning. We’ll plan for a replacement when you’re more stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Today we’re scheduled to replace your G tube. It was already due, and we think it’s a good time to do it while you’re here.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is it safe? I’m worried about more pain afterward.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s a routine procedure. We’ll use local numbing gel. Most patients tolerate it well. We’ll give extra pain meds just in case.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The G tube was replaced successfully. The old one was removed and a new one placed over a guidewire. The site looks clean.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I felt some pressure, but not too bad. How’s the output now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Still high, but we’ll keep monitoring. We’re starting to transition you back to rectal morphine and Phenergan since you’re tolerating things better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Can we increase the morphine? 20 mg isn’t cutting it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re increasing it to 25 mg every 6 hours as needed. We’ll watch for side effects like drowsiness or slow breathing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing better. Pain is down, and you’re off IV meds. We’re keeping you on TPN and your new G tube is working well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m glad. But I’m still anxious about the femoral line. When will it be replaced?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re scheduling it for early next week. It’s important to fix it before it fails completely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your pain is now at a 3-4 with the 25 mg morphine. That’s a big improvement.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, finally something is helping. I’ve even slept a few hours.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great. We’ll keep you on the current plan. Social work stopped by—they said you had a good talk.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it helped. I’m still overwhelmed, but I feel heard.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re planning your discharge later this week. First, we’ll replace your femoral line tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m nervous. Will it be done under sedation?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, you’ll get light sedation—fentanyl and Versed—so you’ll be relaxed and won’t feel much. It’s a quick procedure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that helps. And my other meds will stay the same?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Mostly. The only change is the morphine dose—now 25 mg PR every 6 hours as needed. Everything else continues as before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. You just had your femoral line replaced. It went smoothly—you tolerated it well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I don’t even remember much. Is it secure?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, new catheter is in place, cuff positioned correctly. You can use it right away for TPN and meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Now that the line is fixed and your pain is controlled, we’re ready to discharge you today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good news. What about follow-up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll see your gastroenterologist and pain clinic as scheduled. And please follow up with your psychiatrist—we think that’s important.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. I’ve realized how much the emotional side affects my pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Managing both is key. At home, keep using the 25 mg morphine PR as needed, but hold it if you’re drowsy or breathing slowly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. And my G tube and line care?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Same as before—flush the G tube regularly, care for the skin, and do the ethanol lock for the line daily.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I can manage that. Thank you for listening and adjusting my pain meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. We know this is a chronic struggle. We’re here to support you through each flare-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: It means a lot. I’ll keep in touch with my team.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. We’ll get your discharge papers ready. You should be home within a few hours.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m ready. It’s good to be going home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll make sure you have all your prescriptions updated, especially the new morphine dose.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, please. I don’t want to run out.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’ll be filled before you leave. And if pain worsens, don’t hesitate to call your doctor or come back.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you again for everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well. Take care, and we’ll see you in follow-up if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll stay in touch. I’ve learned to speak up when things aren’t working.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s the best thing you can do. Keep advocating for yourself.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks for respecting that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Of course. That’s how we get the best outcomes—together.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel hopeful. That’s a good place to be.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re glad to hear that. Rest up at home and take it one day at a time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you for the support.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. We’ll make sure your home health nurse is set up to help with your care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I’ve already spoken to them. It’s reassuring.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. We want you to feel supported at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I do. I’m ready to go.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll get the discharge order processed. Safe travels home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I’ll follow up with all my doctors.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. Take care of yourself.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. See you soon, hopefully not in the hospital.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We hope so too. But we’re here if you need us.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s comforting to know.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Always. Rest well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take it easy.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I plan to.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great. We’ll see you in follow-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I’ll be there.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. We’re rooting for you.
